title: Win-rate collapse and conflicting explanations at Harrowgate Industrial Supply

organization.industry: MRO (maintenance, repair and operations) parts and supplies distribution
organization.size: approx. 620 staff; 44 quota-carrying sales reps in 4 regions (North, South, East, West), a 6-person inside-sales desk, a 9-person marketing team and a 3-person revenue-operations (RevOps) team

presentingRequest: Our new-business win rate has fallen from 31% in Q1 to 18% in Q3. Marketing has done its part - leads are up 60% this year - so the problem is in sales. I think the team got comfortable after a strong 2025: follow-up is slow and nobody is pushing deals over the line. I want help designing a sales accountability program: individual win-rate targets, weekly pipeline reviews, and performance improvement plans for any rep under 20% by the end of Q1 2027. - Graham Pellew, CEO

evidence.text: 'Win rate was 31% in Q1 and it's 18% now. Marketing tripled down on lead generation and we have 60% more leads than last year, so this can't be a lead problem. Look at the CRM: touches per opportunity are down about a third, and it takes the team almost a day to call a lead back. That's complacency. They had a great 2025, hit their accelerators, and stopped hustling. The reps will tell you it's the leads or the comp plan - every sales team blames marketing and the comp plan.'

'We switched our purchased-lead vendor from Fieldline Data to LeadSpring on 2026-04-01. LeadSpring costs $38 a lead against Fieldline's $71, and Fieldline wanted a 45% price increase to renew. Lead volume is up 60% and MQLs have nearly doubled. On 2026-04-15 we lowered the MQL threshold from a score of 60 to 40, because LeadSpring's contacts are earlier in the buying journey and we didn't want to waste them. My team delivers more qualified opportunities than ever; sales just isn't closing them.'

evidence.source: Sales reps, focus group of 7 reps from all four regions (2026-10-21)
evidence.text: Rep A: 'Since April, half the people I call downloaded a whitepaper and have never heard of us. They aren't buying anything.' Rep B: 'Every one of those calls becomes an opportunity in the CRM whether there's a need or not, and then it sits there and gets closed lost.' Rep C: 'We call the quote requests first - those are real buyers. The whitepaper people get called when we get to them.' Rep D: 'And the new comp plan cut our pay by about a third. That's why good people are checked out and half the team is looking for jobs.' Several reps nodded at Rep D's comment; none gave figures.

'My reps are working harder than last year, not less. The problem is we can no longer tell a good opportunity from a bad one because everything that picks up the phone becomes an opportunity. In June I asked RevOps to switch off the automatic opportunity creation for low-score leads. I was told no, because MQL-to-opportunity conversion is on marketing's scorecard. I don't know whether LeadSpring's good leads are worse than Fieldline's good leads - honestly, the high-score ones seem about the same to me.'

2026-04-01: Purchased-lead source switched from Fieldline Data to LeadSpring (content-syndication leads). 2026-04-15: (a) MQL threshold lowered from lead score 60 to 40; company-size filter (>=50 employees) removed from the MQL criteria (this filter applied only at the MQL step; every lead, from every source, is scored and recorded in the CRM regardless). (b) New automation: for every MQL reached by phone, a Stage-1 'Qualify' opportunity is created automatically. Previously reps created opportunities manually, only after confirming a defined purchase need. (c) Opportunities with no logged activity for 60 days are closed automatically as Closed-Lost, reason 'Unresponsive'. Lead-scoring model version v4.2 has been in use unchanged since 2025-09-08. Win rate is defined throughout as closed-won / (closed-won + closed-lost) opportunities closed in the quarter; this definition has not changed.

evidence.source: CRM lead-funnel extract by source, Q1 and Q3 2026 (RevOps, 2026-10-14)
evidence.text: Q1 2026: total leads 2,400 = Fieldline 1,500 (55% scoring >=60) + other marketing channels (web forms, webinars, trade shows) 900 (47% scoring >=60). Leads scoring >=60: 1,248 (52%). MQLs under the then-current rule (>=60): 1,248. Q3 2026: total leads 3,840 (+60%) = LeadSpring 3,000 (18% scoring >=60) + other marketing channels 840 (45% scoring >=60). Leads scoring >=60: 922 (24%). MQLs under the then-current rule (>=40): 2,460. Other-channel volume and score distribution in Q3 were within 5% of their Q3 2025 values.

evidence.source: CRM closed-opportunity analysis by source and lead-score band (RevOps, 2026-10-14)
evidence.text: Q1 2026 (all marketing opportunities came from leads scoring >=60, per the rule then in force): Non-marketing sources (referrals, existing-account expansion, rep-sourced) 550 closed, 175 won (31.8%). Marketing, Fieldline 300 closed, 89 won (29.7%). Marketing, other channels 150 closed, 46 won (30.7%). Total 1,000 closed, 310 won (31.0%). Q3 2026: Non-marketing sources 540 closed, 167 won (30.9%). Marketing score >=60, LeadSpring 280 closed, 75 won (26.8%). Marketing score >=60, other channels 150 closed, 43 won (28.7%). Marketing score 40-59 (all sources; 690 of 750 from LeadSpring) 750 closed, 25 won (3.3%). Total 1,720 closed, 310 won (18.0%). Of the 725 lost opportunities in the 40-59 band, 442 (61%) were closed by the 60-day auto-close rule with reason 'Unresponsive'. Excluding the 40-59 band, the Q3 win rate is 285 / 970 = 29.4%.

evidence.source: RevOps quarterly pipeline review, Q3 2026 (analyst notes)
evidence.text: Marketing-sourced win rate (leads scoring >=60) over the five quarters before the vendor switch: Q1 2025 31%, Q2 2025 29%, Q3 2025 33%, Q4 2025 27%, Q1 2026 30%. Non-marketing win rate over the same quarters ranged 29%-33%. A matched comparison of LeadSpring and Fieldline leads by product category and customer size was attempted but could not be completed: LeadSpring records have industry and employee-count fields populated for only 61% of leads, versus 97% for Fieldline. 'We cannot yet say whether LeadSpring's high-score leads close at a different rate from Fieldline's once mix is controlled for.'

evidence.source: CRM activity data per rep, Q1 vs Q3 2026
evidence.text: Quota-carrying reps: 44 in both quarters. Logged activities (calls, emails, meetings) per rep per week: Q1 58, Q3 65 (+12%). Quotes issued per rep per month: Q1 22, Q3 24 (+9%). Open opportunities per rep (average): Q1 23, Q3 39 (+70%). Logged touches per open opportunity per month: Q1 10.9, Q3 7.2 (-34%). Customer-visit meetings per rep per week: Q1 4.1, Q3 4.3.

evidence.source: CRM lead-response data, Q1 vs Q3 2026
evidence.text: Median time from MQL to first rep contact: all MQLs Q1 4 h, Q3 19 h; MQLs scoring >=60 only Q1 3 h, Q3 14 h. Within Q3 marketing opportunities scoring >=60 that closed in the quarter: first contact within 4 h: 150 closed, 50 won (33%); first contact after 24 h: 140 closed, 31 won (22%). Leads flagged 'quote requested' make up 58% of the within-4-h group and 21% of the after-24-h group. The CRM does not record win rate by response time within the 'quote requested' flag.

evidence.source: Payroll and HR records, sales compensation and attrition (Finance/HR, 2026-10-16)
evidence.text: The 2026 sales comp plan (effective 2026-04-01) kept the base commission rate at 4.0% of gross margin, raised the accelerator threshold from 100% to 110% of quota, and added a 90-day clawback on returned goods. Median variable pay per rep, April-September: 2025 $18,400; 2026 $18,900 (+3%). Reps earning less than 70% of their prior-year variable pay for April-September: 3 of 44. Voluntary sales-rep departures April-October: 2025 3; 2026 2.

evidence.source: Sales pulse survey, anonymous (September 2026; 39 of 44 reps responded)
evidence.text: 'Lead quality has gotten worse this year': 74% agree (2025: 22%). 'I spend too much time on opportunities that will never buy': 69% agree (2025: 25%). 'The commission plan is fair': 41% agree (2025: 46%). 'I intend to be working here in 12 months': 81% agree (2025: 83%). Engagement index 68 (2025: 70).

evidence.source: Regional trade press, 'Brannock Supply cuts list prices' (2026-06-12)
evidence.text: Competitor Brannock Supply announced list-price reductions averaging 8% on bearings, fasteners and power-transmission products, effective 2026-06-10, in the North and East regions.

evidence.source: CRM monthly win rate and lost-reason codes, 2026
evidence.text: Overall monthly win rate: January 31%, February 30%, March 32%, April 29%, May 21%, June 19%, July 18%, August 18%, September 18%. Non-marketing-source win rate, April-September, monthly range 29%-32%. Lost reason 'Price' as a share of non-marketing-source losses: Q1 22%, Q3 23%. North+East win rate on non-marketing sources: Q1 31%, Q3 30%.

evidence.source: Finance new-business bookings and RevOps time-log summary, Q1 vs Q3 2026
evidence.text: New-business bookings: Q1 $4.31M (310 won deals); Q3 $4.18M (310 won deals). Q3 average won-deal value: non-marketing $14,900; marketing score >=60 $13,900; marketing score 40-59 $2,100 (25 deals, $52,500 in total). Rep time logged against score 40-59 opportunities in Q3: 1,880 hours (about 43 hours per rep). The inside-sales desk (6 staff) reported 31% unused capacity in Q3 after a distributor-portal project ended in June.

VP Marketing variable compensation: 40% on MQL volume, 20% on MQL-to-opportunity conversion rate, 25% on cost per lead, 15% on brand-awareness survey. No component is tied to closed-won revenue or win rate. Reported MQL-to-opportunity conversion: Q1 2026 36%, Q3 2026 48%.

hypotheses.text: Sales reps have become complacent and reduced their effort since 2025, and this is the main cause of the fall in win rate from 31% to 18%.

The fall in the reported win rate is mainly a change in the mix of opportunities: low-score (40-59) leads admitted to the sales pipeline from mid-April, with opportunities created automatically, now make up a large share of closed opportunities and close at a very low rate.
The switch to LeadSpring and the new MQL criteria have improved the sales pipeline, as shown by 60% more leads and nearly twice as many MQLs.

LeadSpring's leads are intrinsically lower quality than Fieldline's at the same lead score, so that the vendor switch, independent of the MQL criteria change, has lowered the close rate on high-score marketing leads.
The April 2026 comp plan change cut rep earnings and demotivated the sales team, and this is a major driver of the win-rate decline.

edges.from: 2026-04-15 MQL threshold change and automatic opportunity creation
edges.to: Fall in overall reported win rate

edges.from: Slower first rep contact on high-score (>=60) marketing leads
edges.to: Lower win rate on high-score marketing leads

edges.from: Switch of purchased-lead vendor from Fieldline to LeadSpring
edges.to: Fall in the share of leads scoring >=60 (52% to 24%)

actions.text: Implement the CEO's accountability program: individual win-rate targets, weekly pipeline reviews, and performance improvement plans for every rep whose win rate is below 20% at the end of Q1 2027.

Re-baseline win-rate reporting: report win rate by lead source and lead-score band, flag automatically created opportunities, and use the segmented figures (not the blended rate) in leadership reviews and before setting any targets.
Terminate the LeadSpring contract and return to Fieldline Data at its renewal price.

Stop automatically creating field-rep opportunities for leads scoring 40-59; route them to the inside-sales desk or a marketing nurture track, tracking their conversion separately, and review the result after one quarter.
